chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, all together, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: The one who labours over the Qur'an and memorizes it with difficulty on his part and having poor memory - for him is double the reward.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for someone who struggles to memorize the Quran?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the virtue of 'ijtihād al-muthl' (exertion) in Quranic memorization, noting that those who struggle due to a weak memory receive double the reward. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the quality of effort over innate ease, aligning with the principle that spiritual merit is often proportional to the difficulty overcome. The narration underscores the accessibility of divine reward for all believers, regardless of their natural cognitive capacities.

en.ammaar-muslim: [5/1545] al-Kafi: A number of our companions from Ahmad b. Muhammad and Sahl b. Ziyad all together from Ibn Mahbub from Jamil b. Salih from al-Fudhayl b. Yasar from Abi Abdillahعليه السلام. He (Fudhayl) said:
I heard him (i.e. the Imam) say: The one who labours over the Qur’an and memorizes it with great difficulty on his part and having poor memory - for him is double the reward
